root_cause.text: AppArmor’s DFA differential-encoding verification in `verify_dfa()` used a single mark and incorrect iterator-based bailout logic, causing states in the currently traversed chain to be mistaken for already verified states and letting diff-encoding loops evade detection.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly says the code “conflated states that had gone through check and already been marked, with states that were currently being checked and marked” and that the bailout “compared current chain check iterators j,k instead of using the outer loop iterator i”; the patch fixes this by adding a separate `MARK_DIFF_ENCODE_VERIFIED`, checking `MARK_DIFF_ENCODE` as a “loop in current chain”, and removing the old `if (k < j) break; /* already verified */` logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a new DFA flag constant to represent a verified diff-encode mark state.
intent_record.what: A new preprocessor macro named MARK_DIFF_ENCODE_VERIFIED with value 0x10000000 was added alongside the existing DFA match/mark flag definitions, without modifying any other macros in this hunk.
intent_record.how: This introduces a new available bit flag that code can use at runtime to mark a diff-encode state as verified, reserving the 0x10000000 bit for that purpose, but by itself this hunk does not change behavior unless other code begins setting or checking the new flag.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix DFA diff-encode chain verification by separating temporary loop-detection marks from permanent verified marks to correctly detect cycles and preserve validated chains.
intent_record.what: The diff changes the loop condition in verify_dfa() from checking for states not marked with MARK_DIFF_ENCODE to checking for states not marked with MARK_DIFF_ENCODE_VERIFIED, adds an in-loop check that aborts if the current state already has MARK_DIFF_ENCODE set, removes the old 'if (k < j) break' early-exit logic from the first traversal, and adds a second traversal that walks the diff-encode chain again to clear MARK_DIFF_ENCODE and set MARK_DIFF_ENCODE_VERIFIED until it reaches a previously verified chain or exits.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this changes diff-encode chain verification from using a single transient mark to a two-phase marking scheme: one mark detects loops within the currently explored chain, and a separate verified mark records chains that have already been fully validated. This prevents falsely treating in-progress traversal marks as globally verified state, improves detection of self-loops and cyclic chains, and allows later traversals to stop safely when they reach an already verified chain.

relevance_review.reason: The root cause is the verifier’s use of a single mark that conflated 'currently traversing' with 'already verified'. Adding a new DFA flag for a verified diff-encode mark directly supports separating those states, which is part of fixing the loop-detection flaw.

The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes DFA differential-encoding verification by using separate temporary and permanent marks for loop detection versus verified states, addressing the incorrect marking logic that allowed diff-encoding loops to escape detection.

candidates.rationale: This iterator-based bailout assumes any backward reference means the target state was already verified. In diff-encoded chains this is incorrect, because k can point to a state in the current traversal chain, allowing loops to evade detection.

The loop termination uses a single MARK_DIFF_ENCODE bit to mean both 'seen in current walk' and 'already verified'. This conflation is the core root cause: states in the current chain can be mistaken for previously validated states.
This sets the only available mark bit during traversal, permanently conflating temporary loop-detection state with verified state, which enables incorrect acceptance of diff-encoding loops.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement sets the single MARK_DIFF_ENCODE bit during traversal, conflating a temporary 'seen in current chain' mark with a permanent 'already verified' mark. That directly causes states in the active diff-encoding walk to be mistaken for previously validated states, enabling loop evasion.

This loop condition relies on the same single MARK_DIFF_ENCODE bit to decide whether traversal should continue, treating both transient visitation and completed verification identically. That is the core logic flaw described in the root cause.

This bailout assumes a backward reference means the target state was already safely verified. In a diff-encoded chain, k can instead reference a state in the current traversal chain, so this condition contributes to failing to detect loops.
